prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production animation extension of an ADOPTED pixel game character, not a redesign. The attached sheet is the approved design and poses at nearest 4x; use its first standing pose as exact identity, palette, scale and proportions. Same adopted uncanny anonymous androgynous elongated runner, ~8-head proportions: very small featureless gray-haired head, extremely thin long neck and limbs, plain gray sleeveless running shirt, teal shorts, charcoal leggings and pale shoes. Body ~54 native pixels tall. Never a handsome athlete, muscular person, giant head, identifiable gender, hat or dress.
Create only these NEW motion poses: 4 columns x 2 rows. Top row four clear phases of a complete sprint cycle facing RIGHT: near leg extended contact, gathered passing, far leg extended contact, opposite passing. Very long thin limbs unchanged, fixed scale. Bottom row (4) short hit recoil alive, (5) regain balance, (6) awkward short arm jab windup, (7) small forward palm jab with planted feet. No weapons or trails. Tired poses already exist.
Transparent RGBA background, equal grid cells, generous transparent gutters, consistent full-body scale and ground baseline, complete feet and limbs. Clean chunky square pixel clusters for a small game sprite enlarged into the output, same muted palette, 1-pixel native dark brown contour, upper-left illumination. No smooth airbrushed illustration, no labels/grid/text/background/ground shadows/additional people. Same head and face in every cell. Meaningful limb changes, never just translated duplicates. Output only the motion sheet.
